saints.name: St. Bernard of Menthon
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: The archdeacon of Aosta who built the Alpine hospices that sheltered travelers for a thousand years…
biography: Born in 923, by tradition at the castle of Menthon near Annecy in Savoy, Bernard refused an arranged marriage and became a priest under Peter, archdeacon of Aosta, whose office he later inherited. For forty-two years he preached through the mountain villages, his charge including the care of the poor and of travellers.

The passes toward Italy were deadly with snow, cold, and robbers. For the safety of pilgrims and merchants he founded a hostel and a community of canons at the summit of the pass that came to bear his name, the Great St. Bernard, nearly 8,000 feet above the sea, and later a second on the Little St. Bernard. The rescue dogs of the hospice grew famous only in later centuries.

He died at Novara in 1008 and was canonized by Pope Innocent XI in 1681. In 1923 Pope Pius XI confirmed him patron of the Alps; and because his hospices guarded those who climb, ski, or journey in high mountains, he is invoked as patron of mountaineers and of all who travel the heights.
saints.knownFor: The Alpine hospices that sheltered travelers for centuries.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; named patron of Alpinists in 1923 by Pope Pius XI

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 28 May
